versions.localizedDescription:
An AI-friendly iOS/iPadOS automation service. Tell your agent *"My iPhone is running iCTRL at :8200 — figure out how to drive it."* and it reads the on-device manual and takes it from there. Works with any agent that can make HTTP requests: OpenClaw, Hermes, Minis, Claude Code, Codex and others. ## Downloads ### Which IPA do I need? | File | Needed? | What it is | |---|---|---| | `iCTRLUITests-Runner.ipa` | **Required** | The automation engine. It serves the JSON-RPC API that agents and clients call, and must be running. | | `iCTRL.ipa` | Optional | A companion app for tasks on the phone itself:
• mount the Developer Disk Image without a Mac, and remount it after a reboot
• start and stop the runner
• choose who can reach the runner (this device only / LAN / LAN + nearby)
• see and revoke authorized clients
• read the runner's log live | Skip `iCTRL.ipa` if you mount the Developer Disk Image with Xcode or StikDebug, and manage the runner from its notification or a computer. With a free Apple ID you get three sideloaded apps, and SideStore uses one of them. Install StikDebug *or* the iCTRL app alongside the runner, not both. Both IPAs are unsigned for distribution (ad-hoc, no provisioning profile). Sign them when you install: - **Free Apple ID:** the latest SideStore signs and installs them. Older SideStore releases skip the nested `.xctest`, and the runner then crashes on launch. - **Paid account:** `Scripts/sign-ipa.sh -i iCTRLUITests-Runner.ipa` The runner also needs the Developer Disk Image mounted (Xcode, StikDebug or the iCTRL app). The [README](https://github.com/OpenMinis/iCTRL#installation) covers the whole setup. ## What's new since 1.97.1 ### Nearby discovery: no address to type - **Reach the phone without an address.** Turn on **📡 Nearby Discovery** from the runner's notification or the iCTRL app (it needs Remote Access). Clients can then find the phone: - on the LAN, from any OS; - from a Mac over Apple peer-to-peer Wi-Fi (AWDL), with no shared network at all. The phone only needs Wi-Fi switched on, not joined to anything. - **New client commands:** `python3 ictrl_rpc.py scan` lists discovered phones, and `--nearby ""` replaces `--host`. The first call pairs with the phone (approve once on the phone). - **Strict exposure:** - Nothing is announced on the network unless nearby discovery is on. - The AWDL listener accepts peer-to-peer connections only, and the main listener refuses them. - Nearby discovery can be switched **on** only from the phone itself (notification, iCTRL app or USB). - **Self-healing:** - Advertising follows Wi-Fi off and on, and recovers if the interface is recreated. - A failed listener is rebuilt. - The notification says why nearby discovery isn't ready yet (*turn on Wi-Fi*, *allow Local Network*). ### Who can reach the phone, at a glance - **The status notification's first line** shows one of: 🔒 This device only, 🌐 LAN reachable, or 📡 Nearby discoverable. - **The iCTRL app has a Visibility menu:** 🟢 This device only · safe / 🟡 LAN / 🟡 LAN + nearby. - **LAN addresses are real interfaces only.** VPN or proxy tunnel addresses such as `198.18.0.1` are no longer shown as the phone's address. ### Pairing and keys - **Every pairing is approved on the phone.** The "trusted for 10 minutes" shortcut is gone. - **Limits on requests:** - An unanswered request is refused after 60 s. - Only one request waits at a time, with a 15 s cooldown after a refusal. - Requests from the phone itself have their own slot, so a remote caller can't lock them out. - **Check the key.** The prompt shows a key fingerprint that the client also prints; allow only if they match. - **One key per device.** Clients store keys per device, so a phone paired once works over USB, the LAN and nearby without pairing again. An AI-friendly iOS/iPadOS automation service. Tell your agent *"My iPhone is running iCTRL at <ip>:8200 — figure out how to drive it."* and it reads the on-device manual and takes it from there. Works with any agent that can make HTTP requests: OpenClaw, Hermes, Minis, Claude Code, Codex and others.

## Downloads

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `iCTRLUITests-Runner.ipa` | **The automation engine — required.** |
| `iCTRL.ipa` | Optional host app: mounts the Developer Disk Image on the device and starts the runner. Use it *or* StikDebug. |

Both are unsigned for distribution (ad-hoc, no provisioning profile). Sign them when you install:
- **Free Apple ID:** the latest SideStore signs and installs them. Older SideStore releases skip the nested `.xctest`, and the runner then crashes on launch.
- **Paid account:** `Scripts/sign-ipa.sh -i iCTRLUITests-Runner.ipa`

The runner also needs the Developer Disk Image mounted (Xcode, StikDebug or the iCTRL app). The [README](https://github.com/OpenMinis/iCTRL#installation) covers the whole setup.

## What's new since 1.97.0

**iCTRL app**
- The pairing-file import picker now accepts real pairing files. A pairing record is an XML property list, which the picker greyed out before, so it could not be selected when mounting the Developer Disk Image on the device. Thanks to @wynx1123 (#1).

**Runner**
- No functional changes; only the version number moves to 1.97.1.

For the browser control page changes (full screen, floating quick controls, Home Screen app), see [1.97.0](https://github.com/OpenMinis/iCTRL/releases/tag/v1.97.0).

## What's new since 1.96.1

This release is about the browser control page, `GET /remote`: it now works well from another phone, not only from a desktop browser. The API and the iCTRL app are unchanged.

**Plays on iPhone**
- The stream now plays in Safari on iPhone (iOS 17.1 and later). Before, the page stopped with "browser lacks MediaSource".

**Full screen**
- A full-screen mode that leaves only the picture and a floating ball, entered from the button at the top right, the ball's menu or the Display panel.
- In Safari on iPhone (iOS 26 and later) the picture covers the whole screen, running beneath the status bar and Safari's floating toolbar.
- **Add to Home Screen** opens the page as a web app with no browser bars, straight into full screen, with the iCTRL icon. The same icon is the page's favicon.
- A picture setting for full screen: fill the screen (default), whole picture, or stretch. Touches land where the picture is drawn in every mode.
- Action results (tap, drag, home…) are not shown in full screen, so the view looks like the phone itself. Failures still are.

**Controls**
- A translucent floating ball replaces the settings button on phones. Drag it anywhere; it snaps to a side, remembers its place and darkens over a light part of the picture.
- Tapping the ball opens quick controls: Home, Type, Shot, Open app, Connect/Stop, Full screen, More.
- A Display panel to show or hide the device and connection badges, the device health panel and the status bar.
- Screenshots open in a preview with a Download button, at the device's resolution.
- Dragging sideways on the picture no longer also triggers the browser's back/forward swipe.

**Fixes**
- The connection status no longer stays on "waiting for first frame" while the picture is already playing.
- The dimmed backdrop behind the controls sheet now appears.
- Screenshots were JPEG data saved with a `.png` name; the file type now matches.
- The page is served with `Cache-Control: no-cache`, so an installed web app picks up the page of an updated runner.

**Good to know**
- In a Safari tab, taps on the strip under Safari's toolbar go to Safari. Use the Home Screen app, or the "whole picture" setting, when you need the bottom edge of the phone.
- A Home Screen web app keeps its own storage, so it pairs once more the first time.

## Highlights since 1.32.0
- **Settle-aware actions:** taps, scrolls, typing and `open_url` wait until the screen stops changing and report what changed, ignoring motion the action didn't cause (running animations, video, Picture-in-Picture).
- **Bounded accessibility work:** element lookups and taps by ref use capped tree walks, so slow or busy apps can no longer stall the UI queue.
- **Reading screens:** `collect` reads a long list in one call and switches to OCR when the tree is thin; `page_source enhanced:true` adds text drawn in images.
- **Screen-state flags:** system alerts, overlays, loading indicators, login walls, anti-bot checks and promotional popups are reported with each read; refs refuse to act on a screen that has changed.
- **Smoother remote control page (`GET /remote`):** screen capture is several times faster, the stream plays with low latency up to 30 fps, and the page supports horizontal swipes, long press, and right-click for Home.
- **Runner home-screen icon.**
- **iCTRL app:** mounts the cryptex Developer Disk Image on iOS 26.4 and later, detects the LocalDevVPN tunnel by actually connecting through it, and checks network permissions on first launch.

An AI-agent-friendly iOS automation service. Tell your agent *"My iPhone is running iCTRL at <ip>:8200 — figure out how to drive it."* and it reads the on-device manual and takes it from there.

## Downloads

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `iCTRLUITests-Runner.ipa` | **The automation engine — required.** |
| `iCTRL.ipa` | Optional host app: mounts the Developer Disk Image on the device and starts the runner. Use it *or* StikDebug. |

Both are unsigned for distribution (ad-hoc, no provisioning profile). Sign them when you install:
- **Free Apple ID:** the latest SideStore signs and installs them. Older SideStore releases skip the nested `.xctest`, and the runner then crashes on launch.
- **Paid account:** `Scripts/sign-ipa.sh -i iCTRLUITests-Runner.ipa`

The runner also needs the Developer Disk Image mounted (Xcode, StikDebug or the iCTRL app). The [README](https://github.com/OpenMinis/iCTRL#installation) covers the whole setup.

## Highlights
- **Faster:** synthesized taps (~280ms median). Visible-screen reads under 1s even on long feeds. On-device OCR when the accessibility tree is empty.
- **Reliable on busy and backgrounded apps:** queries against an app that has left the screen are refused immediately instead of stalling the UI queue. Abandoned calls can no longer pile up and get the runner killed for CPU use.
- **Better element targeting:** `find_element` prefers on-screen matches and reports `visibility` and `alternatives`. `scroll_to_element` drags straight to known positions and says when an element isn't in the view at all.
- **Controlled from notifications:** long-press to approve pairing, toggle remote access, or stop the server.
- **Builds from a fresh clone** with `make ipa` and nothing but Xcode and XcodeGen.
- **Now licensed under Apache-2.0** (previously AGPL-3.0).

## Highlights since 1.32.0
- **Settle-aware actions:** taps, scrolls, typing and `open_url` wait until the screen stops changing and report what changed, ignoring motion the action didn't cause (running animations, video, Picture-in-Picture).
- **Bounded accessibility work:** element lookups and taps by ref use capped tree walks, so slow or busy apps can no longer stall the UI queue.
- **Reading screens:** `collect` reads a long list in one call and switches to OCR when the tree is thin; `page_source enhanced:true` adds text drawn in images.
- **Screen-state flags:** system alerts, overlays, loading indicators, login walls, anti-bot checks and promotional popups are reported with each read; refs refuse to act on a screen that has changed.
- **Smoother remote control page (`GET /remote`):** screen capture is several times faster, the stream plays with low latency up to 30 fps, and the page supports horizontal swipes, long press, and right-click for Home.
- **Runner home-screen icon.**
- **iCTRL app:** mounts the cryptex Developer Disk Image on iOS 26.4 and later, detects the LocalDevVPN tunnel by actually connecting through it, and checks network permissions on first launch.
